obligations.text: Intended: uninstall <module> removes the installed module's resources and its record from the current namespace.
obligations.cases: successful vs failing resource providers: resolve-children error (C:D27) and editing-locked class delete (C:D28) vs successful providers
obligations.observation: module record and stored manifest; whether the module code remains callable; command status
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (intended promise; iter10/iter11 as-built models contradict it; playbook unin_refines_complete proves it only under successful providers and PGA)

obligations.text: A module name is required unless -all is given.
obligations.cases: uninstall with no name and no -all vs with -all vs with a name
obligations.observation: command refusal before any change
obligations.gap: No model of the Main.cls::Uninstall argument check (Unit/CLI.cls TestUninstallWithoutModuleName is a test only). Contrast: `uninstall` with neither a name nor -all is refused with nothing changed, while `uninstall -all` proceeds.

obligations.text: Uninstall runs without a transaction, so a failure can leave some resources removed.
obligations.cases: uninstall that fails after an earlier deletion (uninstall <m> -r where <m> needs zpm) vs a successful uninstall
obligations.observation: resources present after the failed command; command status
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (playbook witness: the target's code and IPM's classes are deleted, then the command fails with both records kept)

parent.entailment: The parent promises removal of resources and record (P1), the name/-all argument rule and non-transactional failure (B1) beyond its children; these are graded directly. No parent obligation is credited by composition: cleanup#1 holds only under successful providers, and child-error/class-delete-error refute the removal promise.

obligations.text: Uninstall deletes the module's classes, packages, includes and routines with their compiled forms, its record, its stored manifest and its sync baseline.
obligations.cases: code kinds, record, stream and baseline vs kinds that remain (name-only global, declared mapping, ^Sources entry)
obligations.observation: presence of each artifact after uninstall
obligations.basis: reused:.g5/ontology/features/uninstall.g5.md metadata (iter63 cleanup.rs); playbook clean_code/record_delete added in iteration-70

obligations.text: A global resource's data is deleted only when the resource names it with the Global attribute.
obligations.cases: global resource with Global attribute vs name-only global resource
obligations.observation: global data after uninstall

obligations.text: FileCopy targets are deleted on uninstall.
FileCopy targets with KeepOnUninstall are kept.
As built (C:D67), declared <Mapping> entries stay in the namespace after uninstall, also with -purge.
obligations.cases: declared mapping vs removed code kinds; purge vs no purge
obligations.observation: namespace mapping configuration after uninstall

obligations.text: As built (C:D68), a developer-mode module's ^Sources entries stay after uninstall and keep pointing at its old folder.
obligations.cases: ^Sources entry vs removed code kinds; purge vs no purge
obligations.observation: ^Sources entries after uninstall

obligations.text: Uninstall expands a package without selecting resources separately claimed by another stored reference, including a nested package.
obligations.cases: own class vs class claimed by another module vs class inside a nested package another module claims
obligations.observation: which files the clean removes

obligations.text: The checked ASCII names match without regard to case.
obligations.cases: claimed reference spelled with different case vs same case
obligations.observation: whether the differently cased claim protects the class
obligations.gap: Name segments are ints that stand for case-folded provider output, so case-insensitive matching is a premise, not a modeled decision. Contrast: a claim on "a.b" vs files under "A.B" (ResourceReference.GetChildren/IRIS collation) must protect the class; no rule distinguishes case variants.

obligations.text: A separately declared child of the same module is left out of its parent package's expansion, but its own declaration selects it, so uninstall removes it.
obligations.cases: same-module child declared separately vs not
obligations.observation: package children set; files after clean

obligations.text: The checked uninstall removes the selected classes and module record while leaving another module's nested class callable.
obligations.cases: own selected class vs other module's nested class
obligations.observation: files present and module records after clean

obligations.text: When an editing lock prevents a class from being deleted, uninstall prints a warning, reports success and removes the module and manifest records while the class remains callable.
obligations.cases: editing lock held vs not held
obligations.observation: command status and warning; module and manifest records; class presence

obligations.text: Without the lock, the checked uninstall removes the class.
obligations.cases: no editing lock vs lock
obligations.observation: class presence and warning

obligations.text: Intended: without -force, IPM does not uninstall a module that other installed modules depend on.
obligations.cases: dependent whose dependency graph builds vs dependent whose graph fails to build (F-UNIN-4); force vs no force
obligations.observation: target module record after the command
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (proved under premise PG; refuted by the playbook F-UNIN-4 witness, where an unresolvable dependent graph lets the target be removed)

obligations.text: With -force the module is uninstalled despite its dependents.
Intended: the refusal is an error that names the dependents.
obligations.cases: blocked uninstall (dependent present, no force) vs unblocked
obligations.observation: returned status and message
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (as-built models return success for the blocked case; the repaired neighbour returns an error). The message naming the dependents is not modeled.

obligations.text: As built, a blocked uninstall deletes the module's web applications first.
As built, the module's before-Clean hooks (author Invoke hooks and processor OnBeforePhase("Clean") effects other than web-app deletion) run before the dependency check.
obligations.cases: blocked uninstall with a Clean-Before Invoke hook vs no hook
obligations.observation: hook side effects of a blocked uninstall
obligations.gap: playbook before_clean models only WebApplication.cls deletion in Storage/Module.cls::ExecutePhases; author <Invoke Phase="Clean" When="Before"> hooks and CSP purge are excluded (uninstall.TRUST.md U10). Contrast: a blocked uninstall of a module with a Clean-Before Invoke whose effect is observable (e.g. a global set) vs the repaired order where the check runs first.

obligations.text: As built, the command prints "Clean SKIPPED - required by ...", keeps the module and returns success.
Working assumption: a need declared only for a phase (test, verify) does not block uninstall.
obligations.cases: dependent whose need is Scope="test" vs an unscoped need
obligations.observation: whether the target is skipped
obligations.gap: No model of phase-scoped dependencies in Utils/Module.cls::GetDependentsList / BuildAllDependencyGraphs as read by Lifecycle/Base.cls::CheckBeforeClean (playbook graph is data; iter33 dependents.rs has no scope). Contrast: uninstall of A where B declares A only with Scope="test" removes A, while an unscoped need skips it. Open question uninstall.dependents.scoped-policy.

parent.entailment: P1 states the intended rule (graded directly, refuted); B1 restates the as-built child except the before-Clean hooks clause, graded here as absent. No composition credited.

units.B2: excluded: provenance (P:F-UNIN-1, P:F-UNIN-6, C:D25) and the proposed repair C:S17, which is not applied

obligations.text: A blocked uninstall deletes the module's web applications.
obligations.cases: blocked (dependent, no force) vs repaired check-first order
obligations.observation: web applications after the command

obligations.text: A blocked uninstall keeps the module installed and reports success.
obligations.cases: blocked vs forced; as-built vs repaired
obligations.observation: module record and returned status (and its history row)

obligations.text: The dependent module's own applications are untouched.
obligations.cases: resources owned by the target vs by another module
obligations.observation: presence of the dependent's resources
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (playbook l1_only_own: only resources owned by modules in scope are deleted; premise PF concerns shared FileCopy folders only)

obligations.text: -force removes the module despite its dependents.
obligations.cases: force vs no force with one dependent
obligations.observation: module kept or removed

obligations.text: After a forced uninstall the dependent stays installed with its dependency gone.
obligations.cases: dependent record vs target record under -force
obligations.observation: module records after the command
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (l1_only_own: records removed only within scope(t), which excludes dependents)

obligations.text: Intended: -recurse also uninstalls the module's dependencies that no other installed module needs.
obligations.cases: dependency needed only by the target vs needed by another module
obligations.observation: dependency record, stored manifest and code after the command
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (F-UNIN-9 witness: the dependency's code and record go but its stored manifest stays, so the dependency is not fully uninstalled)

obligations.text: With -recurse, a dependency that another installed module still needs is kept installed.
obligations.cases: dependency also needed by another module vs needed only by the target
obligations.observation: dependency record and code after the command
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (its web app is still deleted and its row logged as success: owned by uninstall.dependents.as-built)

obligations.text: -recurse with -force also removes dependencies that other installed modules still need.
obligations.cases: force vs no force for a shared dependency under -recurse
obligations.observation: shared dependency record after the command
obligations.gap: check_skip drops the dependents test under force, but no lemma or witness exercises -recurse with -force (l1_dependents_protect is stated only for !force). Contrast: `uninstall top -r -force` where dep is also needed by other removes dep's record, vs the same without -force keeping it (Lifecycle/Base.cls::%Clean dependency loop, CheckBeforeClean).

units.B3: excluded: classification as C:D27 against the removal promise of uninstall#1 (refutation recorded there)

obligations.text: If a resource processor returns an error while resolving its children, uninstall still reports success and deletes the module and manifest records while leaving that resource's code installed (the failed hook returns before copying its child list and Clean ignores the status).
obligations.cases: hook error vs hook success
obligations.observation: command status; module and manifest records; code presence

obligations.text: Packaging propagates the same resolution error.
obligations.cases: hook error vs hook success
obligations.observation: package status

obligations.text: A successful hook selects the class and the checked uninstall removes it.
obligations.cases: hook success vs error
obligations.observation: code presence after uninstall

obligations.text: -all uninstalls every module in the namespace except IPM itself.
obligations.cases: IPM vs other modules; all modules visited
obligations.observation: installed-module store after the command
obligations.gap: uninstall_all_step is a per-module boolean table; store retention is an input (provider_retained) and IPM's retention is never asserted. No model of Utils/Module.cls::UninstallAll traversal over all installed modules (playbook uninstall.rs excludes it, U9). Contrast: a namespace with zpm, A and B (A needs B) ends with only zpm's record, vs a missed module.

obligations.text: As built, without force, a failed module blocks later attempts on dependencies that still need it.
obligations.cases: provider failure without force vs success
obligations.observation: traversal graph membership; later attempts on the failed module's dependencies
obligations.gap: The failed module staying in the work graph is asserted, but the consequence (its dependencies are not attempted) needs the traversal loop, which is not modeled. Contrast: A fails, B (needed by A) is never attempted and stays; vs A succeeds and B is removed.

obligations.text: As built, with force, IPM removes a failed module from its traversal graph and continues, retaining the error in its final status.
obligations.cases: provider failure with force vs without force
obligations.observation: traversal graph membership; final command status
obligations.gap: The step removes the failed module from the work graph and its step status is not OK, but continuation to later modules and aggregation into the final status of UninstallAll are not modeled. Contrast: with force, A fails, B is still removed and the command returns A's error.

obligations.text: Traversal progress is not proof of removal from the installed-module store: a failed provider can leave resources or its row behind.
obligations.cases: forced failed provider vs successful provider
obligations.observation: work-graph removal vs stored module row

obligations.text: Uninstall skips modules with global scope unless -global is given.
obligations.cases: GlobalScope module with vs without -global
obligations.observation: module record and code after the command
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (playbook: intent_blocked includes global scope; blocked_unchanged under PW and honest under PB; iter59 global_module_skipped shows -global removes the code). The skip leaves web apps deleted when the module owns one (premise PW); see handoff.

obligations.text: Intended: -purge deletes the data in the module's tables during uninstall.
obligations.cases: uninstall with vs without -purge for a persistent-class module
obligations.observation: rows readable after reloading the schema

obligations.text: The pinned implementation leaves table data after uninstall, including with -purge.
An ordinary persistent-class module retains its rows after uninstall with or without -purge, and loading the same schema makes those rows readable again.
obligations.cases: purge vs default flag; before vs after reload; SDK %DeleteExtent neighbour
obligations.observation: SQL row count and value after reload

obligations.text: The command sets Purge while the installer callback receives only Configure.Purge, and ordinary class deletion does not purge its extent.
obligations.cases: -purge vs -DConfigure.Purge=1 vs default; class delete vs extent delete
obligations.observation: callback argument; rows after class deletion

obligations.text: A supported installer can delete its own data: -DConfigure.Purge=1 reaches its callback and deletes its rows, while the same setting without an installer leaves them intact.
obligations.cases: installer callback with Configure.Purge=1 vs Purge=1; no installer
obligations.observation: rows after uninstall; callback argument

obligations.text: `uninstall zpm` removes IPM from the namespace.
obligations.cases: uninstall zpm (with/without force, with/without the full-cleanup answer) vs other modules
obligations.observation: IPM classes and record after the command
obligations.gap: unin_refines_honest gives success iff removed only under PNF (no full cleanup) and PB; no lemma or witness shows `uninstall zpm` actually deleting IPM's classes and record, and the full-cleanup path (Utils/Module.cls::UninstallAll, Lifecycle/Module.cls IPM block) is unmodeled (TRUST U9). The success row is written before Clean (U11). Contrast: `uninstall zpm -force` leaves no %IPM classes, vs a skipped Clean that still reports IPM uninstalled (OBS-H15).

obligations.text: `uninstall zpm` first asks whether to also remove all other modules and IPM's metadata, and then the shell exits. (That the metadata never includes the history log is owned by history.keep-on-ipm-uninstall in concepts/data-policy.)
obligations.cases: exact name zpm with vs without -force; any other name
obligations.observation: prompt shown; self-uninstall exit flag
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (premise PN; F-UNIN-3 witness shows `uninstall IPM` by external name bypasses the guard)
